article.title: How to Replace One Damaged Vinyl Plank
article.summary: Replace a scratched or chipped vinyl plank without redoing the floor: unclick it from the nearest wall, or cut it out in the middle and glue in a new one.
article.body:
Click-lock vinyl plank floors are built so a single plank can be swapped. You can unclick the floor from the nearest wall, or, in the middle of a big room, cut the damaged plank out and glue a new one in. This guide covers both.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: wear safety glasses and cut-resistant gloves. Set any saw depth to the plank thickness so you don't cut the underlayment or subfloor, and check for radiant floor heating first.

Steps

  1. Find a matching plank and let it acclimate

    Use a leftover plank from the original install if you have one, because color can vary between production lots. Leave it in the room for at least 24 to 48 hours, or as the maker says, so it matches the floor's temperature.

    Done right: the new plank's pattern and color match the floor around the damaged one.

  2. Choose your method

    If the damaged plank is within a few rows of a wall, removing the trim and unclicking rows is the cleanest repair. If it's far from any wall, the cut-out method saves you from lifting half the room.

    Done right: you've counted the rows to the nearest wall and picked a method.

  3. Unclick method: lift rows from the nearest wall

    Pry off the baseboard or quarter round along the nearest wall. Lift the first row at an angle to unlock its long edge, then slide planks apart along the short ends. Number them with tape as you go. Work until you reach the damaged plank, swap in the new one, then click the rows back in reverse order.

    Done right: every plank goes back in its original spot and the seams close flat with no gaps.

  4. Cut-out method: remove the damaged plank

    Tape off the planks around it. Cut a line about 1 in inside each edge with a multi-tool or a saw set to the plank's thickness, then cut from the corners to that rectangle. Lift out the center, then work the remaining edge strips out of the neighbors' locks without damaging them.

    Done right: the opening is clean, the surrounding planks' locking edges are undamaged, and the underlayment is intact.

  5. Cut-out method: fit and glue the new plank

    Trim the locking lip off the new plank's long side and one short side with a utility knife, so it can drop straight down into the opening. Test the fit. Apply a thin bead of vinyl seam adhesive to the exposed locks of the surrounding planks, lower the new plank in, and press the seams flat. Wipe off squeeze-out and set weights on it overnight.

    Done right: the plank sits level with its neighbors and the seams are tight once the adhesive cures.

Call a flooring installer if: the damage came from water and the subfloor feels soft, several planks in a row need replacing, or the floor is glued down rather than floating.

FAQ

Can you replace a single vinyl plank?

Yes. Either unclick the floor from the nearest wall to reach it, or cut out the damaged plank and glue in a trimmed replacement.

What if I don't have a spare plank?

Check the manufacturer and product name on leftover boxes or receipts. If it's discontinued, take a plank from inside a closet and replace that one with a close match.

Do I need to remove baseboards to replace a vinyl plank?

Only for the unclick method along the wall. The cut-out method doesn't touch the trim.

Will a glued-in plank stay put?

Yes, when the locks are cleaned and the adhesive is made for vinyl seams. Keep weight on it for the full cure time on the label.
